key_idea: Line 1 rounds m to the nearest whole name_1; line 2 rounds m to the nearest whole name_2 and then splits that integer by c_1, so carries are handled automatically.
sketch: Let P1 = product of all c_i and P2 = product of c_2..c_{n-1}. Rounding half up in integers is (2m+P)/(2P). Print round(m/P1) name_1, then t=round(m/P2) and t/c_1 name_1, t%c_1 name_2. Pitfalls: products can overflow, so cap them at 1e11 (any P > 2m gives 0 anyway) using 128-bit multiplication; for n=2 P2=1 and the second line is exact; unit names are always printed as given (plural). The low solve count on Kattis reflects obscurity, not difficulty.
